# Contributing to Desktop Material

:+1: :tada: :sparkling_heart: Thanks for your interest! :sparkling_heart: :tada: :+1:

The following is a set of guidelines for contributing to Desktop Material, which
is developed in [`Ding-Ding-Projects/desktop-material`](https://github.com/Ding-Ding-Projects/desktop-material).
These are just guidelines, not rules. Use your best judgment, and feel free to
propose changes to this document in a pull request.

Desktop Material is an independent Material Design 3 remake of GitHub Desktop.
It is not a GitHub, Inc. product, and issues or pull requests about it belong on
this repository rather than upstream — see
[Relationship to GitHub Desktop](#relationship-to-github-desktop) below.

Note that Desktop Material is an evolving project, so expect things to change
over time as the project learns, listens and refines how it works with the
community.

## What should I know before I get started?

### Code of Conduct

This project adheres to the Contributor Covenant [code of conduct](../CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
By participating, you are expected to uphold this code.

Please report unacceptable behavior by opening an issue on
[this repository's tracker](https://github.com/Ding-Ding-Projects/desktop-material/issues/new/choose).
The `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` text inherited from upstream names a GitHub, Inc.
address; that address belongs to the upstream project and is not monitored by
Desktop Material, so use this repository's tracker instead.

### Relationship to GitHub Desktop

Desktop Material's codebase originated as a fork of
[`desktop/desktop`](https://github.com/desktop/desktop), which is published under
the MIT licence, and it keeps that licence. That attribution is why the upstream
project is credited throughout this repository's documentation and history.

Attribution is not a support channel. Upstream maintainers cannot triage,
reproduce, or fix anything about Desktop Material, so:

- bugs, feature requests, and pull requests for **Desktop Material** go to
  [this repository](https://github.com/Ding-Ding-Projects/desktop-material/issues)
- a bug you can also reproduce in a released build of **GitHub Desktop** is worth
  reporting upstream as well, since a fix here does not reach GitHub Desktop users

### The Roadmap

See the project's root [`ROADMAP.md`](../ROADMAP.md).
The immediate milestones are more detailed, and the latter milestones are more
fuzzy and subject to change.

If you have ideas or suggestions please read the
[Suggesting Enhancements](#suggesting-enhancements) section below to understand
how to contribute your feedback.

## How Can I Contribute?

### Reporting Bugs

This section guides you through submitting a bug report for Desktop Material.
Following these guidelines helps maintainers and the community understand your
report :pencil:, reproduce the behavior :computer: :computer:, and find related
reports :mag_right:.

Before creating bug reports, please check [this list](#before-submitting-a-bug-report)
as you might find out that you don't need to create one. When you are creating
a bug report, please [include as many details as possible](#how-do-i-submit-a-bug-report).
Fill out the required template, the information it asks for helps resolve issues faster.

#### Before Submitting A Bug Report

**Perform a [cursory search](https://github.com/Ding-Ding-Projects/desktop-material/labels/bug)**
to see if the problem has already been reported. If it does exist, add a
:thumbsup: to the issue to indicate this is also an issue for you, and add a
comment to the existing issue if there is extra information you can contribute.

#### How Do I Submit A Bug Report?

Bugs are tracked as [GitHub issues](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues).

Simply create an issue on the [Desktop Material issue tracker](https://github.com/Ding-Ding-Projects/desktop-material/issues/new?template=bug_report.yaml)
and fill out the provided issue template.

The information we are interested in includes:

 - details about your environment - which build, which operating system
 - details about reproducing the issue - what steps to take, what happens, how
   often it happens
 - other relevant information - log files, screenshots, etc

### Suggesting Enhancements

This section guides you through submitting an enhancement suggestion for
Desktop Material, including completely new features and minor improvements to
existing functionality. Following these guidelines helps maintainers and the
community understand your suggestion :pencil: and find related suggestions
:mag_right:.

Before creating enhancement suggestions, please check [this list](#before-submitting-an-enhancement-suggestion)
as you might find out that you don't need to create one. When you are creating
an enhancement suggestion, please [include as many details as possible](#how-do-i-submit-an-enhancement-suggestion).
Fill in [the template](ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.yaml), including the steps
that you imagine you would take if the feature you're requesting existed.

#### Before Submitting An Enhancement Suggestion

**Perform a [cursory search](https://github.com/Ding-Ding-Projects/desktop-material/labels/enhancement)**
to see if the enhancement has already been suggested. If it has, add a
:thumbsup: to indicate your interest in it, or comment if there is additional
information you would like to add.

#### How Do I Submit An Enhancement Suggestion?

Enhancement suggestions are tracked as [GitHub issues](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues).

Simply create an issue on the [Desktop Material issue tracker](https://github.com/Ding-Ding-Projects/desktop-material/issues/new?template=feature_request.yaml)
and fill out the provided issue template.

Some additional advice:

* **Use a clear and descriptive title** for the feature request
* **Provide a step-by-step description of the suggested enhancement**
  This additional context helps the maintainers understand the enhancement from
  your perspective
* **Explain why this enhancement would be useful** to Desktop Material users
* **Include screenshots and animated GIFs** if relevant to help you demonstrate
  the steps or point out the part of Desktop Material which the suggestion is
  related to
* **List some other applications where this enhancement exists, if applicable**

### Reporting a Security Vulnerability

Security vulnerabilities do **not** go in a public issue. Follow
[`SECURITY.md`](../SECURITY.md), which routes reports through this repository's
private vulnerability reporting form.

### Help Wanted

As part of building Desktop Material, tasks that are good for external
contributors get identified and labelled. These tasks:

 - have low impact, or have a known workaround
 - should be addressed
 - have a narrow scope and/or easy reproduction steps
 - can be worked on independent of other tasks

These issues are labelled [`help wanted`](https://github.com/Ding-Ding-Projects/desktop-material/labels/help%20wanted)
in the repository, and newcomer-sized ones are also labelled
[`good first issue`](https://github.com/Ding-Ding-Projects/desktop-material/labels/good%20first%20issue).
If you are interested in contributing to the project, please comment on the
issue to let the maintainers (and the community) know you are interested in it.
